headline.funnel_interpretation: Egger’s test is generally not recommended when fewer than 10 studies are available.
headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 3 studies yielded an overall effect size of 0.49 (95% CI: 0.35–0.7), suggesting that anti-inflammatory diet is associated with a lower risk of bladder cancer. These findings were supported by low between-study heterogeneity (I² = 17.15%), indicating consistent findings across the included studies.
